rows.title: Introduction to Administration of Justice
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Analyze criminal laws and procedures in the justice system and apply to current events.
Identify and discuss ethical considerations for law enforcement professionals.
Explain and critique the interrelationships among the three core components of the criminal justice system: Courts, Corrections, and Law Enforcement.
Evaluate the history of the justice system and compare the historical theories to contemporary trends in the criminal justice system.
objectives: Identify, explain and discuss the origin of laws in both ancient and modern society.
Analyze and compare laws and justice institutions of other societies with the American system.
Convey understanding of the history, structure, and trends of law enforcement, courts and corrections, in order to identify emerging and future patterns in the criminal justice system.
Identify and discuss ethical considerations for the contemporary law enforcement professional.
Explain and discuss the education and training of the law enforcement professional in the American justice system.
Demonstrate an understanding of the roles and functions of the core components on the US criminal justice system: courts, corrections, and law enforcement.
Critically analyze and discuss issues related to the criminal justice system and crime from various perspectives and scholarly research.
Demonstrate the ability to describe and critique specific issues in the criminal justice system as it relates to special populations, including juveniles.
Effectively write a research paper using APA, ASA or a generally accepted writing format.
Analyze patterns in crime, crime activity, and criminal methods.
Demonstrates and understanding of crime, criminology, and the problem of crime in America.

rows.title: Survey of Art from Prehistory to the Medieval Era
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Identify, examine, and assess representative works of art and architecture from prehistory through the medieval period employing appropriate art historical terminology
Analyze, evaluate, and distinguish materials and techniques used for creating art and architecture from prehistory and medieval period.
Analyze, discuss, and differentiate the roles of art, architecture, and the artist from prehistory through the medieval period
objectives: Identify, examine, and assess representative works of art and architecture from prehistory to the medieval era employing appropriate art historical terminology.
Analyze works of art and architecture in terms of aesthetic, socio-political, religious, historical, technological, and cultural contexts in which they were created.
Develop critical thinking, information literacy, and problem solving through an engagement with art, architecture, artists, and patrons from prehistory to the medieval era.
Part 2
Identify, examine, and assess representative works of art and architecture from prehistory through the medieval period employing appropriate art historical terminology
Analyze, discuss, and differentiate works of art and architecture in terms of historical context and cultural values
Analyze, discuss, and differentiate the roles of art, architecture, and the artist from prehistory through the medieval period
Develop strong writing skills as they relate to analysis of visual forms taught in this course.
Discuss the effect of early art on the gothic era.
Differentiate between art in the Romanesque era and The Byzantine era

rows.title: General Histology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Compare and contrast four mammalian tissue types.
Identify and describe tissue structures and layers of all mammalian organs.
Identify and describe organs based upon tissue arrangement.
objectives: Identify cellular organelles and explain their basic functions.
Identify and differentiate cell types.
Identify and explain the functions of general mammalian tissue types.
Identify, compare, contrast and explain basic functions of tissues as they relate to organ systems.

rows.title: Introduction to Speech
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Create multimedia Informative and Persuasive speeches
Critically evaluate communicated messages in various contexts
Apply communication theories to various contexts, including one's own experiences
objectives: Deliver a variety of individual informative and persuasive speeches before an audience, using rhetorical principles to ensure ethical communication and appropriate audience adaptation.
Develop communication confidence in various contexts, including public speaking.
Analyze communication theories by applying them to one's own experiences.
Relate to other individuals using effective verbal messages, nonverbal messages, and active listening skills.
Formulate effective communication skills in a variety of social contexts for diverse audiences.
Organize and present a variety of individual faculty-supervised, faculty-evaluated speeches delivered to a live audience (one to many).
Retreiving, critically examining, and using supporting materials from primary and secondary sources for credibility, accuracy, and relevance in speeches and presentations.
Demonstrate rheotrical sensitivity to diversity, equity, inclusion, belonging, and accessibility.
Critically discuss and write about human communication theories and events.
Explain and apply the basic concepts of the field of communication.
Discuss the history of the study of human communication.
Compare and contrast the basic research methods for the evaluation of human communication phenomena.
Explain the contextual, cultural, and social foundations of human communication.
Demonstrate a basic knowledge of the specializations comprising the communication discipline.
Demonstrate an understanding of ethical perspectives in communication.
Summarize and explain an expanded world perspective that demonstrates an appreciation of the diverse range of individuals, communities, and viewpoints.

rows.title: History of Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Examine dance making from a historical, political, cultural and social context.
Critically analyze dance as a response to past and present-day social concerns.
Develop analytical and critical skills required to respond, define and write about dance as an academic subject.
objectives: Compose analytical statements about the development in 21st century America
Identify select dance genres in America and internationally
Identify select choreographers in America and internationally
Identify careers in dance in America and internationally
Summarize historical events impacting dance in America and internationally
Discuss Africanisms in American dance
Discriminate genres in contemporary American dance
Discriminate genres in traditional/folkloric dance
Assess form and function in dance
Critic theories and methodologies of major dance icons

rows.title: Emergency Medical Technician–Basic
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Identify and describe the basic anatomy and physiology of the human body.
Identify and describe the roles/responsibilities of the EMT in the pre-hospital setting.
Identify the proper sequence for performing a patient assessment on the sick and injured.
objectives: State the medical/legal issues of emergency care.
Demonstrate advanced CPR.
Assess an injured person for respiratory, neuro, cardiac, renal, skeletal, and tissue injuries.
Take vital signs and make an initial assessment of injury.
Perform emergency childbirth.
Treat shock, burns, and multiple trauma.
Administer to pediatric emergencies.
Demonstrate medical response to environmental/hazardous material emergencies.
Use advanced equipment to rescue trapped victims.
Demonstrate proper use of the defibrillator.
Assist with administration of medications.
Assist with advanced airway management.

rows.title: Elementary French
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Sustain communicative conversations in French in everyday situations.
Apply basic vocabulary and grammatical Structures in culturally proper ways.
Read and write informational texts on everyday topics.
Apply a basic knowledge of the culture and geography of the French-speaking world.
objectives: Demonstrate comprehension of French through oral and written exercises
Produce verbal utterances that communicate effectively in French;
Demonstrate basic written texts;
Formulate correct written text on everyday topics;
Demonstrate culturally appropriate use of the French language.
Demonstrate grammatical structures of language in general;
Demonstrate knowledge of the culture and geography of French-speaking countries;
List vocabulary of everyday activities
List vocabulary of foods
List vocabulary of clothing
Differentiate and properly use the affirmative, negative, interrogative, and imperative forms of verbs
Differentiate and use properly the present, near future, and past tense of verbs
Differentiate between definite articles, indefinite articles and partitive articles
Use the formal and informal “you” in social settings
Discuss the different holidays and leisure activities in Francophone countries
Celebrate the diverse cultures of the Francophone world through exploring food, clothing, holidays, leisure activities and history through conversation and projects

rows.title: Introduction to Humanities
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Students will identify and describe the different humanistic disciplines and put them into historical context, keeping in mind their various socio-cultural functions.

Students will be able to describe the basic elements and principles of the formal analysis of various artistic disciplines, and apply that analysis toward understanding and interpreting various humanistic works (of literature, visual arts, film, music, theater, dance, and philosophy).
Students will be able to articulate personal sensibilities of taste, and be aware of the diverse cultural responses and approaches that exist between people and the arts.
objectives: Discuss various socio-cultural functions of human expression.
Interpret various artistic and humanistic “texts” (works of literature, art, film, music, history, philosophy, etc.)
Describe social movements and historical changes through art.
Support personal opinions about specific artistic and humanistic texts and identify some of the ways those opinions have been derived subjectively.

Analyze some of the ways specific artistic and humanistic texts from different eras and national traditions reflect on the governing ideologies of the specific culture(s) from which the texts originally came.

rows.title: Information Seeking Behavior
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Synthesize evidence from scholarly research to draw conclusions about the relationships between information, power, and social systems.
Apply research design and ethical reasoning to investigate how individuals and groups locate, evaluate, and use information in diverse contexts.
Analyze information-seeking behavior as a social and cultural process using principles and methodologies of the social and behavioral sciences.
objectives: Evaluate competing research findings using evidence-based reasoning grounded in behavioral-science methodology.
Interpret information-seeking patterns in light of systemic inequities, power structures, and social identity factors.
Analyze value systems and ethical considerations (e.g., bias, privacy, censorship, and intellectual property) within social-scientific inquiry related to information use.
Apply principles of research design to investigate how individuals and communities seek, evaluate, and use information.
Explain how social-scientific theories and research methods are used to study information behavior across different populations and contexts.

rows.title: Drawing for Animation
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Create a character bible with model sheets, action poses demonstrating strong silhouettes and line of action.
Develop drawings demonstrating the use of perspective, composition and rendering techniques with a focus on layouts illustrating various camera shots and angles.
objectives: Sketch human and animal figures in action poses.
Evaluate, clean up and adjust drawings for character and layout.
Create a portfolio of drawings.
Design characters based on research.
Design layouts based on different camera angles and related to story.

rows.title: Survey of Nutrition and Dietetics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Identify the legal scope of practice for Nutrition and Dietetic Practitioners, especially in regards to California law
Research and effectively communicate an area of interest regarding career opportunities, job prospects or trends in the industry
Demonstrate knowledge of professional expectations on preparing and compiling a cover letter or personal statement, resume, and job interview expectations
List an overview of the various program/educational requirements, mandatory certification/registration examinations for nutritional professional
objectives: Describe professional ethics and standards of education and practice.
Describe the legal requirements of confidentiality and the dietetics scope of practice.
Describe the scope of practice and credentialing requirements of dietetics professionals at all levels.
Explain the educational and career opportunities in the field of dietetics, clinical management, food service systems, and community nutrition.
Identify the basic content and competencies in the various levels of the profession.
Explain the requirements of the certificate and degrees of the nutrition and dietetics programs.
Plan an academic program with a timeline for completion, including the schedule of supervised practice.
List the required competencies as specified by the Dietary Managers Association and the Commission on Accreditation of Dietetics Programs of the American Dietetic Association.
Develop a career portfolio according to professional guidelines of the American Dietetic Association.
Identify the various titles, credentials and job responsibilities in the field of nutrition and dietetics

rows.title: Introduction to General Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Apply multiple schools of psychology to dream interpretation.
Describe the healthy and unhealthy qualities of your personality type.
Increase awareness of a self-destructive or unhealthy behavior and implement a behavioral modification plan for healthier and more authentic self-expression.
objectives: Assess personality type and connect findings to Freud's ego defense mechanisms and how one deal's with feelings of vulnerability, how to transcend one's ego, and express healthier aspects of personality type.
Explore Carl Jung's archetypes and how they play out in one's life, focusing primarily on the core four archetypes (child, victim, saboteur, and prostitute).
Articulate how one's Adversive Childhood Experiences (ACE) score impacts one's biology.
Use quantum physics principles (alignment of thoughts and feelings) to visualize desired life and identify perceptions that may serve as obstacles to realizing goals.
Apply research methods to specific hypothesis to demonstrate understanding of differences between varying psychological research methods.
Apply dream theories to personal dream to gain potential insight.
Practice and demonstrate dream interpretation skills.
Experiment with mindfulness eating and how it may inform other areas of one's life.
Practice meditation and how it may inform other areas of one's life.
Address areas where one may have conformed to society standard and obeyed authority figure and pros and cons of doing so.
Apply skills and information learned throughout class to stressful life situation to gain a deeper understanding of personal choice and response to situation.
Identify behavior to modify and make healthier by tracking data and applying principles of operant conditioning.
